text:
sam park: quick update 0m canary for v4-quant4. seeing lots of shallow drops across many slices (0.2-1.5% each) that individually are fine but collectively look bad on our dashboard. Thinking of a 'regret budget' approach rather than per-slice hard thresholds. open to feedback.

anita rao: define regret budget? sounds like cumulative but with decay?

sam park: exactly. idea: assign each slice a regret = max(0, baseline - variant) * traffic_share. maintain a rolling budget that decreases when regret accumulates and slowly replenishes over time (decay). trigger progressive mitigation when budget crosses bands (warn, partial fallback, full rollback).

diego martinez: how do you pick decay rate? also how to handle latency improvements that offset regret?

sam park: decay tuned to expected noise: e.g., budget replenishes 10% per hour. latency improvements are accounted for via a convertible credit: latency_gain_weight * latency_reduction added to budget (or used to offset regret). makes it a single scalar economic signal.

irene cho: we should weight regret by slice importance (business slices vs generic). traffic_share alone misses small but high-value slices. propose composite weight = traffic_share * importance_factor. importance_factor from model-registry tags.

anita rao: agree. also want per-customer tier overrides (enterprise slack more tolerant).

sam park: yep, per-customer tier is a field. sketching config below (pseudo):

```
{
  "policy": "regret-budget",
  "window_minutes": 60,
  "budget_capacity": 0.05,        // normalized budget units (5%)
  "replenish_rate_per_minute": 0.0016, // ~10% per hour
  "slice_weight": "traffic_share * importance",
  "latency_credit_factor": 0.7,  // 70% of latency gain converts to budget
  "bands": {
     "warn": 0.6,      // 60% of capacity -> alert but no action
     "partial_fallback": 0.85,
     "rollback": 0.95
  },
  "partial_fallback_steps": [0.2, 0.5], // route 20% then 50% to fallback before full rollback
  "cooldown_minutes": 45
}
```

anita rao: partial_fallback_steps are great. add jitter and a minimum observation window between steps to avoid flip-flop.

diego martinez: operational question 0s metric export granularity required? we need per-slice deltas and importance factor live. @ops-bot

ops-bot: metrics: per-slice deltas exported to metrics.store every 30s. importance_factor currently stored in model-registry and available via lookup. can enable 10s export if needed.

irene cho: how do we handle multi-metric regret (e.g., mrr + qos + hallucination rate)? combine into a single regret scalar via user-defined weights, then budget applies to that scalar. must store weights in model-registry.

sam park: yes, will make multi-metric support the default: regret = sum_k weight_k * positive_delta_k * slice_weight. will include default weights but allow overrides in registry.

anita rao: simulation request: i'll run a backtest on last 45 days for v4-quant4 with budget cap 5% and replenish as above, and produce expected weekly trigger frequency and time-in-partial-fallback. give me a ticket.

diego martinez: logging: capture top 10 slice contributors on trigger and full time series for audit. also emit signed_regret and absolute_regret for debugging.

irene cho: model-registry fields to add: policy_name, policy_config_hash, expected_false_trigger_rate, metric_weights_link. we should also snapshot the exact config in rollout history for reproducibility.

sam park: will draft PR to rollout-service with a unit test that simulates noise and latency credits. ben's earlier idea of per-slice caps still useful to avoid one slice nuking budget.

anita rao: sim ETA 3 hours, will attach results to ticket #ML-7892.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary window start=1744452000 for v4-quant4. health checks: p95 latency, error-rate, regret-budget policy. partial-fallback enabled.

sam park: thanks. i'll monitor the partial fallback steps and watch for high-value slice regressions. ping if we cross warn band. :eyes:

diego martinez: one more ask 0% of the team should have manual override flag to abort automatic steps during major sales events. add to rollout ui.

irene cho: noted. adding to UX ticket.

anita rao: sim complete 045-day backtest: with capacity 5% and replenish 10%/hr expected weekly rollback prob ~0.4%. partial-fallback engaged in 1.8% of trials, median time-to-recovery 25 minutes. uploading plots to ticket.

sam park: perfect. i'll include the sim summary in the model entry and proceed with the canary. thanks all. :rocket:
